grade.summary: The submission gives a complete proof. The integer-valued potential Φ strictly decreases whenever the selected numbers have nontrivial gcd, while in the coprime case Φ stays constant and the number k of entries greater than 1 strictly decreases; this supplies a valid lexicographic termination argument. It also correctly proves that k never falls below 1, so the terminal board has exactly one entry greater than 1. Primewise, the move applies the Euclidean transformation (e,f) ↦ (min(e,f),|e−f|), preserving the gcd of all p-adic exponents. At termination this invariant equals v_p(M), uniquely determining M from the initial board.
strengths: Correctly analyzes every possible change in the number of entries greater than 1.
Provides a valid finite integer monovariant together with the secondary parameter k.
Correctly identifies and proves the primewise exponent-gcd invariant.
Reconstructs the terminal value M explicitly, establishing independence of all choices.
